items.title: Bolivia's defense minister resigns amid weeks of mass protests

featured_image.name: Bolivia's defence minister resigns after weeks of mass protests | Reuters

items.description: Bolivia's Defense Minister Marcelo Salinas resigned on Tuesday after a month of anti-government protests that have blocked roads and cut off access to major cities, a ministry source confirmed to Reuters. The departure marks the highest-level exit from President Rodrigo Paz's government since unrest engulfed the country in early May.[1][2]

items.title: Trump endorses Colombia presidential candidate De La Espriella

featured_image.name: Right-wing candidate pulls ahead in Colombia's presidential vote

items.description: U.S. President Donald Trump on Tuesday endorsed Abelardo De La Espriella, a right-wing lawyer seeking Colombia's presidency, inserting himself into a polarized Latin American contest ahead of a June 21 runoff election. Trump posted on Truth Social that the outcome of the vote "is crucial for the future of Colombia and its ties with the United States," according to Reuters.[1][2]

items.title: IRGC strikes US Fifth Fleet headquarters in Bahrain

featured_image.name: Iran's IRGC attacks US Fifth Fleet headquarters, airbase, local media  reports | Reuters

items.description:
Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps launched missile and drone attacks on the U.S. Fifth Fleet headquarters in Bahrain and an airbase in a neighboring country on Tuesday, in what Tehran described as retaliation for American strikes on a communications tower south of Qeshm Island, according to Reuters and Iranian state media.[1][2]

The IRGC's naval forces also targeted a vessel identified as the Panaya with missiles, claiming the strike was a response to a U.S. attack on an Iranian tanker near the Strait of Hormuz that allegedly damaged the ship's engine room. "Endangering the security of the Strait of Hormuz will result in significant repercussions for the U.S. military," the IRGC said, according to Iranian media.[3][1]

items.title: Rubio says Netanyahu's plan to seize 70% of Gaza contradicts US vision

featured_image.name: Rubio says Netanyahu's goal to seize 70% of Gaza contradicts ...

items.description:
Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's directive to expand military control over the Gaza Strip to 70% has drawn a rare public rebuke from the Trump administration, with Secretary of State Marco Rubio telling lawmakers on Tuesday that the plan contradicts the U.S. vision for the territory.

"We have a plan. It doesn't call for that," Rubio said during congressional testimony when pressed on Netanyahu's announcement, according to Anadolu Agency. The remarks, made during back-to-back hearings on Capitol Hill, represent one of the clearest signals of daylight between Washington and Jerusalem on Gaza policy.[1][2][3]

items.title: US fires Hellfire missile at tanker heading to Iran

featured_image.name: US blockade: Missile cripples crude oil tanker M/T Lexie, preventing it  from reaching Iran's Kharg Island

items.description:
U.S. Central Command announced Tuesday that a U.S. aircraft fired a Hellfire missile into the engine room of the Botswana-flagged tanker M/T Lexie after its crew ignored repeated warnings over a 24-hour period while transiting international waters toward Iran's Kharg Island oil terminal.[1][2]

The strike marks the sixth commercial vessel disabled since CENTCOM began enforcing its naval blockade of Iranian ports on April 13, with U.S. forces having redirected 122 other ships attempting to enter or exit Iranian ports during that period.[1]

items.title: Kuwait condemns 'repeated' Iranian missile and drone attacks on its territory

featured_image.name: Kuwait condemns Iranian attacks on its territory as flagrant violation of  sovereignty, security

items.description:
Kuwait's Cabinet on Tuesday issued a strong condemnation of what it called "repeated Iranian missile and drone attacks" targeting Kuwaiti territory, describing the strikes as dangerous provocations and affirming the country's full right to defend its sovereignty.[2]

The statement followed two separate incidents — the first on Friday, May 29, when Kuwaiti air defenses responded to missile and drone strikes following US operations against Iranian drones, and a second on Monday, June 1, when Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) launched missiles targeting US forces stationed in Kuwait.[3][2]

items.title: Kremlin demands Ukraine cede territory hours after deadly mass attack

featured_image.name: Russia launches massive drone and missile attack on Ukraine, killing 3 in  Kyiv - OPB

items.description: Hours after Russia unleashed one of the largest aerial attacks of its full-scale invasion, Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov declared on Tuesday that the war could end within 24 hours if Ukrainian forces withdrew from Donbas and other Russian-occupied territories. Ukrainian media outlet NV described the statement as a "cynical ultimatum," noting its timing in the wake of strikes that killed dozens of civilians across Ukraine.[1]

items.title: UNICEF says Iran war delaying lifesaving aid for children

featured_image.name: Iran war disruption threatening delivery of lifesaving supplies for children,  UN says | Reuters

items.description: The United Nations children's agency warned on Tuesday that surging global transport costs and supply chain disruptions linked to the war in Iran are threatening the delivery of lifesaving aid to children worldwide, with some shipments delayed by up to six months.

items.title: Bahrain bans citizens from traveling to Iran and Iraq

featured_image.name: Bahrain bans citizens from traveling to Iraq, Iran over 'tense security  situation'

items.description: Bahrain's Interior Ministry on Tuesday banned citizens from traveling to Iran and Iraq until further notice, citing "continued security tensions" in the region. The decision comes as the Shiite Muslim holy month of Muharram approaches, during which millions of Shiites traditionally travel to Karbala in Iraq for pilgrimage.[1][2][3]

items.title: Russia kills at least 17 in massive overnight barrage on Ukraine

featured_image.name: Kyiv comes under intense air attack

items.description:
Russia launched one of the largest combined aerial attacks of its full-scale war against Ukraine overnight into Tuesday, firing 73 missiles and 656 drones at cities across the country, killing at least 13 people and wounding more than 100, Ukrainian officials said.[1][2][3]

The assault, which began Monday evening, targeted Kyiv, the central city of Dnipro, Kharkiv, and other areas including Poltava and Zaporizhzhia, according to Ukraine's air force. Ukrainian air defenses intercepted 40 missiles and 602 drones during the onslaught.[4][5][6]

items.title: Israeli strikes kill 8 in Lebanon a day after Trump announced ceasefire

featured_image.name: Trump says Israel and Hezbollah agree to halt hostilities, Lebanon invasion

items.description:
Israeli drone strikes across southern Lebanon on Tuesday killed at least eight people, including a father and his two children struck in a vehicle, even as hostilities were supposed to be winding down following a U.S.-brokered understanding announced just hours earlier, according to the Washington Post.[1]

The strikes came one day after President Trump declared on social media that Israel and Hezbollah had agreed to halt their attacks on one another, with Israel committing not to send troops into Beirut and Hezbollah pledging to stop shooting. The Lebanese army separately confirmed that two of its soldiers were moderately wounded in an Israeli drone strike on a road between the towns of Habboush and Deir al-Zahrani in the Nabatieh area. The Israel Defense Forces did not immediately comment on that incident.[2][3][4]

items.title: Trump berated Netanyahu in expletive-laden call over Lebanon escalation, Axios reports

featured_image.name: Trump loses his temper with Netanyahu in expletive-laden ...

items.description:
President Donald Trump lashed out at Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu in an expletive-laden phone call on Monday, accusing him of jeopardizing fragile US-Iran negotiations with Israel's escalating military operations in Lebanon, according to Axios.[1][2]

During the heated exchange — described by one official as among Trump's worst calls with Netanyahu since returning to office — the president yelled "What the f*** are you doing?" and called Netanyahu "crazy," according to two US officials familiar with the conversation. A US official summarized Trump's remarks: "You're f***ing crazy. You'd be in prison if it weren't for me. I'm saving your a**. Everybody hates you now. Everybody hates Israel because of this".[3][2][1]

items.title: Hundreds protest US Ebola quarantine facility in Kenya

featured_image.name: Protesters demonstrate the Ebola treatment center established or Americans in Kenya

items.description:
Hundreds of young people took to the streets of Nanyuki, Kenya, on Monday to protest the establishment of a U.S. Ebola quarantine facility at the nearby Laikipia Air Base, days after a Kenyan High Court ordered the project halted pending judicial review.[1][2][3]

The demonstrations in the central Kenyan town came as public anger intensified over the Trump administration's plan to send Americans exposed to Ebola to Kenya rather than repatriating them for treatment on U.S. soil. Protesters constructed barricades and demanded the facility be shut down by June 9, protest leader Patrick Wahome told Reuters.[2][3]

items.title: Takaichi urges Iran to restore free passage through Hormuz

featured_image.name: Japan PM Takaichi Urges Passage of Vessels Through Hormuz in Call With Iran  - Bloomberg

items.description: Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi on Monday called on Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian to demonstrate flexibility in Tehran's negotiations with the United States and to swiftly restore free passage through the Strait of Hormuz for vessels of all nations, according to Japan's Foreign Ministry.[1][2]

items.title: Russia launches major strike on Kyiv, setting apartment buildings ablaze

featured_image.name: Ukrainian capital Kyiv under attack from Russian drones, missiles,  officials say

items.description: A large-scale Russian aerial assault struck Ukraine's capital early on Tuesday, June 2, setting residential buildings on fire and forcing thousands of residents into metro stations and shelters, as Moscow follows through on its threat to conduct "systematic strikes" on Kyiv.

items.title: Frederiksen secures third term as Denmark's PM with new centre-left coalition

featured_image.name: DENMARK-ROYALS-SUMMER TOUR

items.description: Denmark's Social Democratic leader Mette Frederiksen announced on Monday that she has agreed to form a centre-left coalition government, ending more than two months of political uncertainty following the country's March 24 snap election. The deal secures Frederiksen's third consecutive term as prime minister and positions her to continue navigating a diplomatic standoff with U.S. President Donald Trump over the future of Greenland.[1][2][3]

items.title: EU climate chief says COP summits falling short of science

featured_image.name: Climate summits are falling short of what the planet needs, EU climate  chief says | Reuters

items.description:
European Climate Commissioner Wopke Hoekstra said on Monday that the outcomes of most recent United Nations COP climate summits have fallen short of the ambitious action scientists say is needed to tackle climate change, according to Reuters.[1][2]

The remarks, made in Brussels, come one week before the start of the Bonn Climate Change Conference (SB64), scheduled from June 8 to 18 in Germany, which is seen as a critical juncture for the multilateral climate system to demonstrate it can deliver on commitments made at COP30 in Belém last November.[3][4]

items.title: Iran cuts off U.S. talks, vows to fully block Hormuz

featured_image.name: TOPSHOT-IRAN-US-ISRAEL-WAR

items.description: Iran suspended negotiations with the United States and declared its intent to completely shut down the Strait of Hormuz, dramatically escalating a months-long standoff that has already pushed global oil inventories to record-low territory and raised the specter of crude prices surging past $150 per barrel.

items.title: Anthropic confidentially files for IPO after $965B valuation

featured_image.name: Anthropic IPO 2026: Why Claude Mythos Has Investors ...

items.description: Anthropic announced Monday that it has confidentially submitted a draft registration statement on Form S-1 to the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission, taking its first formal step toward a potential initial public offering of its common stock. The filing positions the Claude AI maker ahead of rival OpenAI in the race to go public among the trio of mega-IPOs expected this year.[1][2][3]

items.title: Anthropic files for IPO after $965B valuation

featured_image.name: Anthropic's Valuation Jumped to Nearly $1 Trillion. Here's ...

items.description:
Anthropic announced on Monday that it has confidentially submitted a draft Form S-1 registration statement to the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission, advancing one of the most anticipated public offerings in technology history. The filing follows the AI company's $65 billion Series H funding round, closed on May 28, which valued the Claude maker at $965 billion — eclipsing rival OpenAI's last reported valuation of $852 billion.[1][2]

The company did not disclose the size, pricing, or timing of any potential offering, stating that the IPO would depend on market and other conditions. Industry observers expect a listing as soon as this fall, which would make Anthropic the third in a trio of mega-IPOs reshaping public markets in 2026, alongside SpaceX and OpenAI.[3][4]
